title: Rewrite One Stretch Of A Trading Plan
statement:
Day i has price prices[i] and a planned action strategy[i]: -1 means buy (you pay the price), 0 means hold, 1 means sell (you receive the price). The plan's profit is the sum of strategy[i] × prices[i] over all days. Nobody checks whether you own anything when you sell.

You may rewrite the plan at most once: pick k consecutive days (k is even). The first k / 2 of them become hold (0) and the last k / 2 become sell (1). Days outside the stretch keep their action.

Return the largest profit you can reach. Keeping the plan unchanged is allowed.

examples.why: Rewrite days 1–2: the buy at 2 becomes a hold and day 2 sells at 8. The plan becomes [1, 0, 1, 0]: 4 + 8 = 12.
Every rewrite turns a sell into a hold and loses money, so the original plan (17) wins.
The stretch is the whole array: [0, 0, 1, 1] earns 1 + 6. The first half becomes hold, not buy, so it costs nothing.

hints: Compute the original profit once. How does rewriting one stretch change it?
For the stretch starting at l: subtract what the old actions earned inside it, then add the prices of its second half. Both are range sums.
Prefix sums of strategy[i] × prices[i] and of prices[i] give each stretch's value in O(1). Or slide a window of length k and update both sums as it moves.

explain.intuition:
The rewrite only touches k days, so think of it as a correction to the original profit. For a stretch starting at l, the new profit is base − (old earnings inside the stretch) + (sum of prices in its second half), because the first half now earns 0 and the second half earns its prices.

Both pieces are range sums. With two prefix-sum arrays, each of the n − k + 1 possible stretches costs O(1), and the answer is the best of them and base itself.
steps: Build prefix sums earn[i] of strategy[j] × prices[j] and price[i] of prices[j] for j < i.
For every start l from 0 to n − k: value = base − (earn[l+k] − earn[l]) + (price[l+k] − price[l+k/2]).
Keep the maximum and return it.
pitfalls: Forgetting that the rewrite is optional. When every stretch makes things worse, the answer is the original profit.
Adding the new sells without removing the old earnings of the stretch. An old buy in the stretch must stop costing money, and an old sell must stop earning.
Treating the first half as buys instead of holds.

solutions.title: Recompute every stretch
solutions.idea: For each start, rebuild the plan's profit by walking the stretch day by day.

solutions.title: Prefix sums
solutions.idea: Two prefix arrays turn the old earnings of the stretch and the prices of its second half into O(1) range sums.

followups: Do it in O(1) extra space by sliding a window of length k and updating the two sums as it moves.
Allow up to two non-overlapping rewrites. What extra state do you need?
